DECISION: When no browser clients are connected to the WebSocket server, pre-tool-use returns HTTP 200 with empty body instead of blocking or auto-denying.

IMPLEMENTATION:
- Added `hasClients()` to ws-server.ts: `return (globalThis.__wss?.clients?.size ?? 0) > 0`
- In pre-tool-use route: `if (!hasClients()) { return new Response(null, { status: 200 }) }` before the approval logic
- Claude Code treats empty 200 as 'no opinion' and falls back to its own terminal approval

WHY: Don't block the workflow when the boss isn't watching. If Pixel Office window isn't open, Claude Code should handle approvals normally in the terminal — not hang forever waiting for a WebSocket client that isn't there.

REJECTED: Auto-approve when no clients (security risk). Auto-deny when no clients (breaks workflow).
